en.p: As shown in the figure, there is a tetrahedron $\mathrm{ABCD}$ with $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}=\overline{\mathrm{CD}}=4$ and $\overline{\mathrm{BC}}=\overline{\mathrm{BD}}=2\sqrt{5}$. For the foot $\mathrm{H}$ of the perpendicular from point $\mathrm{A}$ to line $\mathrm{CD}$, the two planes $\mathrm{ABH}$ and $\mathrm{BCD}$ are perpendicular to each other, and $\overline{\mathrm{AH}}=4$.

Let $\mathrm{G}$ be the centroid of triangle $\mathrm{ABH}$, and let $S$ be the sphere centered at $\mathrm{G}$ that is tangent to plane $\mathrm{ACD}$. Let $T$ be the figure formed by all points $\mathrm{P}$ on sphere $S$ with $\angle\mathrm{APG}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. What is the area of the orthogonal projection of figure $T$ onto plane $\mathrm{ABC}$? [4 points]
